cosy-lesson.title: Standing in the Way of Control

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: control – The power to influence or direct people's behavior or the course of events.

p.em: Example: Standing in the way of control means demanding autonomy over your own body and future.

cosy-blockquote.p: survive – To continue to live or exist, especially in spite of danger or hardship.

p.em: Example: We will survive even when institutional systems try to suppress our rights.

cosy-blockquote.p: truth – The quality or state of being true; real facts or reality.

p.em: Example: Speaking truth to power is the cornerstone of effective civil rights movement.

cosy-blockquote.p: friends – People with whom one has a bond of mutual affection and solidarity.

p.em: Example: Leaning on trusted friends provides strength when resisting injustice.

cosy-blockquote.p: trying – Making an effort to achieve something difficult; difficult or annoying.

p.em: Example: Keep trying even when victory seems far out of reach.

cosy-blockquote.p: resistance – The refusal to accept or comply with something; the attempt to prevent something.

p.em: Example: Organized resistance can dismantle oppressive laws and norms.

cosy-blockquote.p: autonomy – The right or condition of self-government and personal independence.

p.em: Example: Bodily autonomy is a fundamental human right that must be defended.

cosy-blockquote.p: freedom – The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without hindrance.

p.em: Example: Freedom is not given freely; it is fought for and maintained by brave people.

cosy-blockquote.p: unity – The state of being united or joined as a whole in purpose.

p.em: Example: Demonstrating unity gives marginalized groups a powerful collective voice.

cosy-blockquote.p: justice – Just behavior or treatment; fairness in society and law.

p.em: Example: Demanding justice requires persistent advocacy and community action.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Share whether you agree or disagree with these statements and discuss them with your teacher:

ul.li: Incorrect: They are standing in the way for control → Correct: They are standing in the way of control ((Use 'in the way of' when indicating an obstacle or resistance to something.))
Incorrect: It is the only way for survive → Correct: It is the only way to survive in this system ((Use 'to + infinitive' after 'way'.))
Incorrect: They fought about their autonomy → Correct: They fought for their autonomy ((Use 'fight for' when advocating for a right, cause, or freedom.))
